concepts.description_formal: If f is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b), then there exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) equal to the quotient of f(b) minus f(a) over b minus a.
concepts.description_plain: On a closed interval where a function is continuous and differentiable inside, some interior point has instantaneous rate equal to the average rate.
concepts.name: Mean Value Theorem as an existence result

concepts.description_formal: If f is continuous on [a,b], then f attains at least one minimum value and at least one maximum value on [a,b].
concepts.description_plain: A function continuous on a closed interval attains both a smallest and a largest value somewhere on that interval.
concepts.name: Extreme Value Theorem as an existence result

concepts.description_formal: c is a critical point of f when f'(c) equals zero or f'(c) fails to exist; all local extrema occur at critical points, and not every critical point is a local extremum.
concepts.description_plain: A critical point is an input where the derivative is zero or does not exist, and being a critical point does not by itself make a point extreme.
concepts.name: Critical points and the local versus global distinction
concepts.notation: critical point; relative extremum; absolute extremum

concepts.description_formal: On an interval contained in the domain of f, f' positive implies f increasing and f' negative implies f decreasing.
concepts.description_plain: Where the derivative is positive the function rises, and where it is negative the function falls.
concepts.name: Monotonicity read from the sign of the first derivative

concepts.description_formal: If f' changes from positive to negative at c then f has a relative maximum at c; from negative to positive gives a relative minimum; no sign change gives neither.
concepts.description_plain: A critical point is a relative maximum or minimum according to how the sign of the derivative changes there.
concepts.name: First derivative test for relative extrema

concepts.description_formal: For f continuous on [a,b], the absolute extrema occur among the critical points in (a,b) together with a and b; comparing f at all of these locates them.
concepts.description_plain: The largest and smallest values of a continuous function on a closed interval are found by comparing its values at every critical point and at both endpoints.
concepts.name: Candidates test for absolute extrema on a closed interval

concepts.description_formal: The graph of f is concave up on an open interval where f' is increasing, equivalently where f'' is positive, and concave down where f' is decreasing, equivalently where f'' is negative.
concepts.description_plain: A graph bends upward where the derivative is increasing and downward where the derivative is decreasing.
concepts.name: Concavity as the monotonicity of the first derivative

concepts.description_formal: The graph of f has a point of inflection at c in the domain of f when f'' changes sign at c.
concepts.description_plain: A point of inflection is where the bending direction actually changes, not merely where the second derivative is zero.
concepts.name: Point of inflection as a change of concavity
concepts.notation: point of inflection; sign change of f''

concepts.description_formal: If f'(c) equals zero and f''(c) is negative, f has a relative maximum at c; if f''(c) is positive, a relative minimum; if f''(c) equals zero the test is inconclusive.
concepts.description_plain: At a critical point where the derivative is zero, the bending direction settles whether the point is a high point or a low point.
concepts.name: Second derivative test at a critical point

concepts.description_formal: When f is continuous on an interval and has exactly one critical point there, and that critical point is a relative extremum, it is the absolute extremum of f on that interval.
concepts.description_plain: If a continuous function has only one critical point on an interval and it is a relative extremum, it is also the extreme value on the whole interval.
concepts.name: A sole relative extremum as an absolute extremum

concepts.description_formal: Zeros and sign changes of f' locate extrema and monotonicity of f; extrema of f' and sign changes of f'' locate the points of inflection of f.
concepts.description_plain: The shape of a curve can be drawn from where its derivative is positive, negative, or turning, and the derivative can be drawn from the curve.
concepts.name: Graph of a function reconstructed from its derivative graphs
concepts.notation: graph of f; graph of f'

concepts.description_formal: Key features of the graphs of f, f', and f'' correspond: zeros of f' to extrema of f, extrema of f' to points of inflection of f, sign of f'' to concavity of f.
concepts.description_plain: A single scenario may present any of f, f prime, and f double prime as a graph, a table, or a formula, and every feature of one constrains the others.
concepts.name: Simultaneous reading of a function and its first two derivatives

concepts.description_formal: Given an objective quantity and a constraint relating the variables, substitution reduces the objective to a single variable function whose extremum on the contextual domain answers the question.
concepts.description_plain: An applied maximum or minimum question becomes a calculus question once one quantity is written as a function of one variable on a stated domain.
concepts.name: Optimisation model with an objective and a constraint

concepts.description_formal: The extreme value of the objective and the input at which it occurs carry the units and the meaning of the modelled quantities.
concepts.description_plain: The answer to an applied optimisation question is a statement about the situation, with units, not only a number.
concepts.name: Interpretation of an optimal value in context

concepts.description_formal: For a relation in x and y, points where dy/dx equals zero or fails to exist are critical points; the second derivative is in general a relation among x, y, and dy/dx.
concepts.description_plain: A curve defined by an equation in two variables has critical points and bending, found from the derivative expression obtained implicitly.
concepts.name: Critical points and behaviour of an implicit relation
